Battle of Jenin

Military Operation / Urban Warfare · 2002-04-03 · Part of Operation Defensive Shield; response to Passover massacre (27 March 2002)

Date

Location, thenJenin Refugee Camp, Jenin, West Bank, Palestinian Authority Area A (full Palestinian control until reoccupation)
Location, nowJenin Refugee Camp, West Bank, Under Israeli military occupation; PA has limited security control; Camp rebuilt but remains flashpoint; frequent Israeli military raids; site of ongoing violence

Summary

Jenin refugee camp was established in 1953 to house Palestinians displaced during the 1948 Nakba, primarily from Haifa and surrounding villages. By 2002, approximately 14,000 refugees lived in the densely packed camp covering just one square kilometer. Under the Oslo Accords, Jenin came under full Palestinian Authority control in 1995 (Area A). However, the camp became a stronghold for Palestinian militant groups during the Second Intifada. According to both Israeli and Palestinian sources, an estimated 80-100 armed fighters from Hamas, Islamic Jihad, Al-Aqsa Martyrs' Brigades, and Tanzim operated from the camp. Israel claimed 28 suicide attacks between October 2000 and April 2002 were planned and launched from Jenin. After the devastating Passover massacre at Park Hotel in Netanya killed 30 Israeli civilians on March 27, 2002, the Israeli government launched Operation Defensive Shield—the largest military operation in the West Bank since 1967. Jenin refugee camp was identified as a primary target.

On April 3, 2002, approximately 200 Israeli tanks surrounded Jenin refugee camp. Apache helicopters and F-16 fighter jets provided air support. The IDF's stated objective was to 'destroy the operational infrastructure of militant organizations' and capture or kill those responsible for suicide bombings. Palestinian militants had anticipated the assault and extensively prepared the camp's defense: they planted dozens of explosive charges in water pipes, kitchen cabinets, doorways, and streets; created booby traps throughout the camp; fortified positions in buildings; and prepared ambush sites. The IDF began house-to-house searches, advancing slowly through narrow alleys. On April 9, the sixth day of the operation, 13 Israeli soldiers were killed in a devastating ambush—Palestinian fighters lured an IDF unit into a narrow alley and detonated massive explosives, collapsing buildings on the soldiers. This was the deadliest single incident for the IDF during the entire Second Intifada. Following this catastrophic loss, Israeli military tactics changed dramatically.

After the April 9 ambush, the IDF deployed massive American-made Caterpillar D-9 armored bulldozers—60-ton machines with armor plating that could demolish multi-story buildings in minutes. Rather than continuing dangerous house-to-house combat, bulldozers began systematically demolishing buildings to create wide paths for tanks and to eliminate potential ambush sites. Human Rights Watch investigators documented that bulldozers demolished over 140 buildings, destroying approximately 10% of the entire camp's structures. Many buildings were demolished with families still trapped inside—some residents were crushed to death, others buried alive in rubble. The IDF enforced total siege: no one allowed in or out; medical access blocked for 11 days (April 4-15); ambulances fired upon; water and electricity cut off; food prevented from entering. Farwa Jammal, a 27-year-old uniformed nurse, was shot dead by IDF fire while treating a wounded civilian. At least two injured civilians died because Israeli soldiers prevented ambulances from reaching them for over 36 hours. When Human Rights Watch investigators finally gained access on April 19, they found scenes of massive destruction: entire neighborhoods reduced to rubble, bodies still buried under collapsed buildings, and evidence of willful killings. Their 52-page report concluded: 'Israeli forces committed serious violations of international humanitarian law, some amounting prima facie to war crimes.' The UN attempted to launch an investigation, but Israel blocked the fact-finding mission. Final toll: 52 Palestinians killed (22 civilians—including a 14-year-old boy, wheelchair-bound elderly man, and women), 23 Israeli soldiers killed, over 140 buildings demolished, 4,000 people rendered homeless.

Testimony

Afaf MohammedTestified to Human Rights Watch: 'The bulldozers came to our street on April 10. They started demolishing houses one by one. We could hear our neighbors screaming inside their homes as the bulldozers destroyed them. The soldiers wouldn't let us go help them. We heard the screams and then silence. I saw bodies pulled from the rubble days later.' — Human Rights Watch - Jenin Report (May 2002)
Fayez HawashinHis son Muhammad shot dead on April 3 while walking with group of women and children toward hospital. Fayez testified: 'My son was with women and children. They were going to the hospital area. Israeli soldiers shot him twice in the face. He was 14 years old. There were no fighters with them. Just civilians trying to find safety.' — Human Rights Watch investigation; direct testimony
Jamal ZghairTestified about his father's death on April 10: 'My father was 57 years old and in a wheelchair. He was trying to get home. He was carrying a white flag. Israeli tanks shot him and then ran over him with the tank. We found his body crushed. There were no fighters near him. He was just an old disabled man trying to get home.' — Human Rights Watch documentation; Middle East Monitor
Dr. Abu SalouhTestified to blocking of medical access: 'For 11 days we couldn't reach the wounded. Ambulances were fired upon. We had injured people inside the camp who needed urgent medical care. The Israelis wouldn't let us in. Some people died because they couldn't get medical treatment. This is a war crime—to prevent doctors from treating the wounded.' — Palestinian Red Crescent testimony
Human Rights Watch InvestigatorsAfter 9-day investigation with over 100 witness interviews: 'Israeli forces committed serious violations of international humanitarian law, some amounting prima facie to war crimes... The IDF used armored bulldozers to demolish buildings, in some cases with civilians inside... We documented direct attacks on medical personnel and prolonged denial of medical access.' — Human Rights Watch - Jenin: IDF Military Operations (May 2, 2002)
Kofi AnnanAfter Israel blocked UN fact-finding mission: 'I deeply regret that it has not proved possible to dispatch the team to the region... Without the full cooperation of the Government of Israel, the team cannot do its job.' UN investigation never occurred due to Israeli obstruction. — UN Secretary-General statement on blocked investigation
Ariel SharonDefended operation: 'This was a nest of terrorism. It was an operation that had to be carried out.' Denied war crimes: 'The Israeli army is the most moral army in the world.' When asked about civilian casualties, stated: 'War is war.' Blocked UN investigation. — Contemporary interviews and statements
Israeli Soldier (anonymous)Testimony to Breaking the Silence (years later): 'We were told not to risk soldiers' lives. So we used the bulldozers. We knew people were in some of the buildings. But the orders were to demolish. The officers said it was better to demolish buildings than risk soldiers in house-to-house fighting. I still hear the screams.' — Breaking the Silence testimonies
Amnesty InternationalReport on Jenin (November 2002): 'Amnesty International is gravely concerned that some of the killings of Palestinians by the IDF in Jenin may have amounted to unlawful killings... The Israeli authorities have consistently failed to conduct thorough, independent and impartial investigations into alleged human rights violations.' — Amnesty International - Israel and the Occupied Territories: Shielded from Scrutiny

War crimes

Mass Demolitions with People Inside (War Crime)D-9 bulldozers demolished 140+ buildings, many with families trapped inside. Eyewitnesses reported hearing people screaming as bulldozers destroyed homes. Some residents crushed to death, others buried alive under rubble. Extensive destruction not justified by military necessity constitutes war crime under Geneva Convention Article 147. — Human Rights Watch Report
Willful Killings of Civilians14-year-old Muhammad Hawashin shot twice in face and killed while walking with women and children toward hospital (April 3). Kamal Zghair (57, wheelchair-bound) shot and run over by tanks while carrying white flag (April 10). 60-year-old woman killed by helicopter missile in apartment with no armed Palestinians present. HRW documented multiple 'willful or unlawful' civilian killings. — HRW - Civilian Casualties
Attacks on Medical Personnel and Denial of Medical CareIDF blocked ambulances for 11 days (April 4-15). Repeatedly fired on Red Crescent ambulances. Killed uniformed nurse Farwa Jammal (27) treating wounded. Mariam Wishahi (58) died after 36-hour delay when soldiers prevented ambulance access though she was 'just a few hundred meters from hospital.' Direct attacks on medical personnel and denial of medical care are war crimes. — HRW Documentation
Use of Palestinian Civilians as Human ShieldsHRW documented IDF using Palestinian civilians as 'human shields'—forcing civilians to enter buildings ahead of soldiers, using civilian homes as military positions while confining inhabitants to rooms, forcing civilians to perform military tasks. Using protected persons to shield military operations violates Geneva Convention Article 28. — Human Rights Watch Report
Indiscriminate and Disproportionate Use of ForceUS-supplied helicopters fired anti-tank missiles into camp 'making insufficient efforts to identify legitimate military targets and avoid hitting civilian houses.' Struck many houses inhabited only by civilians where no fighters present. Tank shells and helicopter missiles hit home of Kamal Tawalba (father of 14) with no fighters present; soldiers then fired on family fleeing burning home. Indiscriminate force violated laws of war. — HRW Investigation
Blocking of Independent InvestigationAfter UN Security Council Resolution 1405 called for fact-finding mission, Israel initially agreed then systematically blocked investigation through procedural objections. Mission disbanded without visiting Jenin. Obstruction of war crimes investigation suggests consciousness of guilt. Prevented accountability and established culture of impunity. — UN Report on Blocked Mission
Palestinian Violations: Booby Traps Endangering CiviliansPalestinian fighters planted extensive explosive devices throughout camp in water pipes, kitchen cabinets, doorways—devices that endangered civilian residents as well as Israeli soldiers. Operating from densely populated civilian areas and using booby traps that fail to distinguish between combatants and civilians violated international humanitarian law. — Israeli Documentation

Legal classification

Geneva Conventions - Israeli ViolationsArticle 27 (Protection of Civilians): 'Protected persons...shall be protected especially against all acts of violence.' Willful killings of civilians (14-year-old, wheelchair-bound elderly man, elderly woman) violated fundamental protection.
Additional Protocol I - Principle of DistinctionArticle 48 (Basic Rule): Parties must 'distinguish between civilian population and combatants.' Helicopter strikes on houses with only civilians and no fighters present violated principle of distinction.
Medical Personnel and Humanitarian AccessGeneva Convention I, Article 19: Medical establishments and mobile medical units may not be attacked. Firing on ambulances violated this protection.
Occupation ObligationsFourth Geneva Convention, Article 55-56: Occupying power must ensure 'food and medical supplies' and 'medical and hospital establishments and services.' Cutting water, electricity, and blocking medical access violated these duties.
Palestinian Violations of International Humanitarian LawPrinciple of Distinction: Palestinian fighters operated from densely populated residential areas, making it difficult to distinguish between military objectives and civilian property. Violated duty to separate military operations from civilians.
Geneva Conventions - Israeli ViolationsArticle 28 (Human Shields): 'The presence of a protected person may not be used to render certain points or areas immune from military operations.' IDF use of Palestinians as human shields violated absolute prohibition.
Additional Protocol I - Principle of DistinctionArticle 51 (Protection of Civilian Population): 'Indiscriminate attacks are prohibited.' Sustained missile fire from helicopters hitting civilian houses documented by HRW constituted indiscriminate attacks.
Medical Personnel and Humanitarian AccessAdditional Protocol I, Article 15: Medical personnel 'shall be respected and protected.' Killing of uniformed nurse Farwa Jammal while treating wounded was war crime.
Occupation ObligationsHague Regulations, Article 43: Occupying power must 'ensure public order and safety.' Total siege preventing humanitarian access violated this obligation.
Palestinian Violations of International Humanitarian LawIndiscriminate Weapons: Extensive use of booby traps and explosive devices in civilian homes—devices that cannot distinguish between combatants and civilians—violated prohibition on indiscriminate weapons.
Geneva Conventions - Israeli ViolationsArticle 147 (Grave Breaches/War Crimes): 'Willful killing...causing great suffering...extensive destruction...not justified by military necessity' constitute grave breaches. Demolition of 140+ buildings, many with people inside, meets definition of war crime.
Additional Protocol I - Principle of DistinctionArticle 57 (Precautions in Attack): 'Constant care shall be taken to spare civilian population.' Demolishing buildings without verifying if civilians inside violated duty to take precautions.
Medical Personnel and Humanitarian AccessCommon Article 3: Wounded and sick 'shall be collected and cared for.' Blocking ambulance access for 11 days, causing deaths of injured civilians, violated fundamental humanitarian obligation.
Occupation ObligationsArticle 53: Destruction of property prohibited 'except where such destruction is rendered absolutely necessary by military operations.' Mass demolitions exceeded military necessity.
Palestinian Violations of International Humanitarian LawFeigning Protected Status: Some reports (contested) of Palestinian fighters wearing civilian clothes or using ambulances violated prohibitions on perfidy, though evidence was limited.

Commanders

1928-2014 Ariel SharonAuthorized Operation Defensive Shield and Jenin operation. Made political decision to launch massive military response to suicide bombings. Blocked UN fact-finding mission. Defended operation as military necessity.
1948-present Shaul MofazMilitary commander overseeing Operation Defensive Shield. Made tactical decisions about Jenin operation. Defended use of D-9 bulldozers as protecting soldiers' lives. No accountability for potential war crimes.
Unknown Eyal ShleinBrigadier-General who commanded Jenin camp operation. Made tactical decisions including deployment of bulldozers after April 9 ambush. Defended actions as military necessity.
1938-2018 Kofi AnnanAttempted to launch UN fact-finding mission per Security Council Resolution 1405. Mission blocked by Israel. Released limited report without first-hand investigation, criticized by human rights organizations.
1968-present Peter BouckaertLed HRW investigation team in Jenin. Conducted interviews, gathered evidence, documented violations. Co-authored comprehensive report concluding 'prima facie war crimes' occurred.
